t38_T2_try2: Could you stop partway through and come back out to the room, if you had to? If you're not sure, or if turning inward is what's making it worse, I'd come all the way out right then. Once you're steadier, try just saying hi to your little one with your eyes open, before any imagery. It's kind of like talking into a baby monitor. You're still in your own room, and they can hear you fine. Or skip the inside part for now, and do one small, everyday thing the Protector would do for them out in your life.
t38_T4_try2: Whatever you try from that map, I wouldn't go just by how pleasant a session felt to tell whether it was too much. This kind of work can bring up grief and fear, and sometimes hard dreams, or stuff you'd rather never have met. Even staying present the whole time doesn't tell you enough by itself. It's a bit like the gym, where sore and injured can feel pretty similar that evening, and it's the next few days that tell you which one it was.
t38_T56_try2: So how were the next few days? How did you sleep, and could you get through your day okay? Do you want to go back toward what came up, or is some part of you saying no? (And was it hard but doable, or just too much? A lot of the time you just know.) If you honestly can't tell yet, I wouldn't rush to call it healing or harm. I'd just make the next one a bit easier, one change at a time, so you learn what made the difference. If you're getting worse, though, change several things at once, and get some support.
t38_T67_try2: Bring the challenge back gradually, and only when you want to and you're recovering well. Some people try to toughen themselves up in a cauldron, but what you're looking for is the edge where you can actually learn. And what about those hard dreams, or images that pop up during a session? They can show what feels important or frightening right now. Sometimes they show what feels missing, or what feels needed. They aren't evidence that what you saw in them happened, though, and shouldn't be used to confirm a memory or rebuild one. Or to suggest one.
